speakers: Cem Karsan (co-host, volatility trader; captioned 'Jim kasang')
summary: Top Traders Unplugged 2024 year-end panel of nine systematic investors (part 1). Main conclusions: slow, big-market trend beat fast trend in a policy-expectation-driven, whipsaw year; index vol selling and structured products pinned volatility and correlation; crowding is real but untimeable; illiquid markets add diversification rather than stronger trends; CTA dispersion stems from speed, universe, purity and size.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the Market moves particularly in fixed income and currencies have been driven by expectations for monetary policy
claims.claim: In 2024 moves in bonds and currencies were driven by shifting monetary-policy expectations rather than sustained trends, so the only big trend was equities plus a few commodities.
claims.conditions: years when rates/FX trade on Fed expectation swings
claims.testable: partly - can measure trend strength by asset class in 2024

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: our slow Trend factor is actually up 12% and a 10v fast factor is down 10 or 11%
claims.claim: In 2024 slow trend following beat fast trend following by over 20 points, so reacting to short-term noise was punished.
claims.indicator: CTA style factors: slow trend factor vs fast trend factor
claims.direction: long slow trend over fast trend in 2024
claims.conditions: choppy years with one large slow trend
claims.testable: yes - compare slow vs fast trend returns 2024

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: larger markets like you know the S&P ET Etc actually worked quite a lot better for Trend this year so our size Factor you know also um suggested larger markets did better
claims.claim: In 2024 trend following worked better in large, liquid markets than in smaller ones, per a market-size style factor.
claims.direction: large markets outperformed small markets for trend
claims.testable: yes - trend returns by market size bucket

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: correlation was actually negative so negative correlation Factor
claims.claim: The correlation style factor for trend was negative in 2024, i.e. trend in more correlated markets did worse.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: This Bitter spot in between whereby you're a bit fast but not too fast you're a bit slow but not too slow that by the time you're short the market recovers
claims.claim: In a fast V-shaped selloff and recovery (August 2024) very slow and very fast trend systems were fine, but medium-speed systems went short at the bottom and lost on the rebound.
claims.direction: medium-speed trend short at the trough then whipsawed
claims.conditions: fast V-shaped reversals within a month
claims.testable: yes - simulate trend speeds through Aug 2024 and similar V events

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we know exactly how it operate in this environment and I don't think we should just go back and reig the models
claims.claim: A single bad event like the August V-shape is not a reason to refit trend models, since the behaviour is known and refitting to one event overfits.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: reversion Dynamics played out quite well uh and I'm talking about crosssectional reversion Dynamics
claims.claim: Cross-sectional reversion strategies did well in 2024 (and, per a later remark, 2023), and skew dynamics helped in commodities and equities around August.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: in the early part of the Year volatility selling kept on being a good rewarded
claims.claim: Volatility selling earned a good premium in early 2024 but less in the second half.
claims.direction: short vol paid H1, less H2
claims.conditions: calm markets; hurt after August vol spike
claims.testable: yes - short-vol index returns by half-year

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the appetite has been and remains brok carry maybe a bit more um conservative following August
claims.claim: After the August 2024 unwind, investor appetite for carry trades became more conservative.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: replication is tends to be a bit slower than the overall industry because we don't have stop losses and fall controls
claims.claim: Managed-futures replication de-risks more slowly than CTAs because it lacks stops and vol controls and uses a rolling window mixing old-regime data, so it lags at inflection points but avoided whipsaw in August.
claims.direction: replication underperforms at turn, then recovers
claims.testable: yes - compare replicator vs SG CTA in Aug 2024

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it just felt to me that simple worked a lot better this year that it was that that the major markets tended to be more stable
claims.claim: In 2024 simple trend approaches in major markets worked better than complex ones because major markets were more stable.
claims.testable: partly - compare simple vs complex CTAs

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: this to them is an incredibly unusual year in that it's been like taking two steps forward and two and a half steps back on across a ton of different trades
claims.claim: A large managed-futures fund reported 2024 as a year of repeated trend reversals across many trades (gains followed by bigger give-backs).
claims.testable: partly - measure trend give-backs per trade

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: it was an election year and there was massive liquidity pumped into the system as is often the case during election years that's very V suppressing supportive for markets
claims.claim: Election years tend to bring large liquidity injections that suppress volatility and support markets.
claims.testable: yes - vol and liquidity in election vs non-election years

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: there's been massive amount of V selling um at the index level um in the S&P 500 throughout the year
claims.claim: Heavy index-level volatility selling on the S&P 500 in 2024 suppressed index volatility.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: structured product issuant go from approximately 500 billion globally to a trillion dollars per year of structured product issu
claims.claim: Global structured product issuance doubled in two years to about USD 1 trillion a year, adding to volatility supply.
claims.direction: more vol supply, lower implied vol

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: ETF tied to yield uh going from in the last two years from uh 25 billion to about 200 billion
claims.claim: Yield/option-income ETFs grew from about 25bn to about 200bn in two years, a further source of systematic volatility selling that pins the index.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: even when we did get the Vol up it reverted very quickly because in the US index ball Supply was incredibly uh well supplied
claims.claim: When US index volatility is heavily supplied by sellers, vol spikes (like August 2024, which came from overseas) mean-revert quickly.
claims.conditions: while index vol supply is abundant

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: if the index is well supplied and pinned in idiosyncratic where still exists things have to start moving away from each other by definition
claims.claim: When index vol is pinned by sellers while single-stock vol persists, implied correlation between stocks must fall, so vol selling drives low correlation.
claims.indicator: implied correlation; index vs single-stock vol
claims.testable: yes - implied correlation vs vol-selling flows

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: the structur product issuance I believe is a secular Trend that is not going away
claims.claim: Structured-product issuance is a secular trend, so index vol supply and low correlation should persist into 2025, while the liquidity driver is less reliable.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan (captioned 'Jim')
claims.quote: if the number one and number two economies uh can get over that divide that will change a lot of things globally
claims.claim: Whether the Trump administration softens or hardens its China stance, given closer Russia-China coordination, is a key geopolitical swing factor for global markets.

claims.speaker: unclear (unattributed in captions)
claims.quote: how do you incorporate geopolitics in a trend following model
claims.claim: For a trend follower geopolitical views do not enter the model; prices already carry the effect, so market observation and trading should be kept separate.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: lighthous are very much in favor of getting the deficit down in favor of a weaker [L180] dollar
claims.claim: Trade policy figures favouring a weaker dollar conflict with a Treasury Secretary who needs a stable dollar to fund the deficit, so dollar direction depends on which voice dominates.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: yields had been rising have have steadied since that appointment
claims.claim: Treasury yields stabilised after Bessent's appointment because markets expect him to steady tariff, dollar and deficit policy.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: for the last 10 years just to put it in context I have seen can year returns betweenus 7 and plus 17% okay this year it's 44
claims.claim: Single-stock cross-sectional momentum (winners minus losers) returned about 44% in 2024 versus a -7% to +17% range in the prior 10 years, driven by mega-cap/AI concentration.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: calling the shots is extremely impossible right and we know the story
claims.claim: Crowded trades can be identified but the timing of their unwind is practically impossible to predict.
claims.testable: partly - test crowding measures as timing signals

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there's much utilization of those strategies and maybe there is some sort of concentration risk coming along which by the way I I I definitely don't see
claims.claim: Press concern about concentration risk in bank QIS strategies is not supported by the data he sees.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's ctas oh it's Vol scaling oh isk parity
claims.claim: After the August 2024 reversal, blame was placed on CTAs, vol scaling and risk parity, and option-overwriting active ETFs have grown sharply; he asks whether these crowding concerns are overstated.
claims.indicator: CTA, vol-target, risk-parity and call-overwriting ETF flows

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the co- movement factor that we look at for Trend was not really a big you know a big factor this year it was really a speed factor that was the biggest differentiator
claims.claim: For trend returns in 2024 the co-movement (crowding) factor mattered little; speed was the main differentiator.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: active uh ETF you know volumes have gone up by orders of magnitude
claims.claim: Active ETF volumes, including managed-futures ETFs, have grown by orders of magnitude.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: if you use it a use the crowding measure and you reduce your positioning it [L240] would have been a very negative
claims.claim: Cutting positions on a crowding signal would have hurt in 2024 because the coordinated positioning kept working.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: the more of all compression you have I think 2017 that was the lowest realized and implied volatility in history
claims.claim: The longer and deeper volatility compression from vol selling, the larger the eventual vol explosion (May-July 2024 compression before August; 2017 record low vol before Volmageddon).
claims.testable: yes - vol level vs subsequent spike size

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: positioning particularly of dealers that that we watch uh is very correlated to Trend so the more the more uh you have a trend and things work the more people Pile in
claims.claim: Dealer positioning tracks trends: as trends work more participants pile in, building concentration like potential energy that raises the size of the eventual blow-up.

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: we are in a period of significant Vault compression happening currently uh really started post election it will probably go through January
claims.claim: Post-election vol compression should last through January 2025; be cautious after the 20 January inauguration and new presidential cycle.
claims.direction: vol low until Jan, risk of rise after Jan 20

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if you can get something like that in a reasonably efficient way then and and you have the fee budget like why not allocate your dollars to people who are doing really really really esoteric things
claims.claim: If core managed-futures beta can be obtained cheaply (replication, QIS, ETFs), fee budgets should go to managers doing esoteric, differentiated strategies.
claims.testable: partly - compare alt-market vs core CTAs net of fees

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they found the best opportunities in the semi-liquid markets like it was the markets where you were in essence coming as a liquidity provider
claims.claim: In semi-liquid commodity markets the best opportunities came from providing liquidity, mean reversion and information asymmetries against non-economic players, not trend.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: do you see strong evidence that they Trend [L280] more
claims.claim: Open question whether alternative (less liquid) markets trend more strongly and implementably after costs; anecdotally, alternative-market managers had historic losses in 2024.
claims.testable: yes - trend returns by liquidity after costs

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you just think about me reversion as kind of like Market making at a slower time frame then you got anything with kind of bigger spreads is going to be kind of wondering around
claims.claim: Mean reversion is like slow market making, so less liquid assets with wider spreads and uncertain fair value offer more mean-reversion profit.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I've never really actually seen any evidence that um less liquid markets do Trend more
claims.claim: In futures there is no statistically significant evidence that less liquid markets trend more; he rejects the slow-information-diffusion story for it.
claims.testable: yes - trend Sharpe by liquidity, same period

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: because the less liquid markets [L300] have of got less history and it just so happens that the less history coincides with the period when trend of falling generally was better
claims.claim: Studies showing illiquid markets trend more are biased because their short histories coincide with good trend periods; compare markets over the same window.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: in crypto it's the reverse like less liquid coins seem to to Trend worse
claims.claim: In crypto less liquid coins appear to trend worse, and in stocks the liquidity-trend evidence is mixed.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: for me the benefit of alss is purely that that you get more diversification
claims.claim: The benefit of alternative markets in trend following is only extra diversification, not stronger trends.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: some of the smaller players um have done particularly well this year and this is on the back of some of these idiosyncratic outliers um you know cocoa coffee Ojo Bitcoin
claims.claim: In 2024 smaller trend managers trading alternative markets profited from idiosyncratic outlier trends in cocoa, coffee, orange juice, Bitcoin and yen crosses.
claims.indicator: cocoa, coffee, orange juice, Bitcoin, GBPJPY
claims.testable: yes - trend returns in those markets

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the dominant markets um I think tend to be much more correlated um than some of the alternative assets
claims.claim: Dominant markets are more correlated with each other than alternative assets, so alternatives add diversification amid a global financial decoupling.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: infant markets tend to be um uh show this prevalence towards trending um conditions and as um as they mature
claims.claim: Young markets tend to trend; as they mature and attract diverse institutional participants they become noisier, more mean-reverting and more efficient (Perry Kaufman).
claims.testable: yes - trend strength vs market age

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I put this down to generally a significant regime shift that occurred from about two 20120 onwards
claims.claim: A regime shift from about 2020 (QE to QT) has produced more idiosyncratic outlier trends, which favour classic, widely diversified trend followers.
claims.conditions: post-2020 QT regime; need broad diversification

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: one market doesn't make a big impact anymore when you trade uh that many markets
claims.claim: Managers trading several hundred markets did not benefit from 2024 outliers because each market is too small a weight; the winners traded few markets.
claims.testable: yes - simulate universe size vs concentration

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: high valued stocks had traded at a at a [L360] higher premium to to lowly valued stocks for for for a kind of a longer periods of time
claims.claim: Asness argues markets have become less efficient: valuation spreads between expensive and cheap stocks have stayed wide for longer than history suggests (as in 2000).

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: due to various factors indexing the low rate environment which you previously had and possibly the impact of social media blunting the wisdom of the crowd
claims.claim: Indexing, low rates and social media have reduced independent views and made markets less efficient, so quant strategies face longer drawdowns but larger eventual opportunities.
claims.testable: partly - drawdown length of value over time

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: it's always a joint hypothesis it's a hypothesis of whether the markets are efficient and the model you use to determine whether there's efficiencies
claims.claim: Market efficiency can only be tested jointly with a valuation model, which is feasible in equities but not in commodities without a valuation anchor.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: for a lot of asset classes the reason why Trend following is effective is because we don't have good valuations so often times you have to use price as your uh measure
claims.claim: Trend following works in many asset classes because there are no good valuations, so price itself is the best gauge (Samuelson: micro efficient, macro inefficient).
claims.testable: partly - trend vs value strength by asset class

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: there's often a disconnect between just analyzing the Topline data in terms of the differences between growth and value
claims.claim: Long-run academic factor studies miss structural change in companies, e.g. big tech now allocates capital better than stock pickers, so old relationships may not hold.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: from a capital allocation and stock investor perspective I think that side of it has in fact become more efficient
claims.claim: Stock picking has become more efficient: persistent bad companies are fewer and activist targets are now good companies, so the low-hanging fruit is gone.
claims.testable: partly - activist target quality over time

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan
claims.quote: the inputs to supply and demand are those flows are increasingly uncorrelated uh unrelated to fundamentals
claims.claim: Prices drift further from fundamental value because most flows now come from non-fundamental sources (central bank and Treasury liquidity, options and structured products, retail, passive).
claims.indicator: central bank liquidity, Treasury liquidity, options flows, passive flows
claims.testable: partly - share of non-fundamental flows vs mispricing

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: personally for me the answer has been know I've not found a serious use for it
claims.claim: Rob has found no serious use for AI in systematic trading.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: you find out that there might be sometimes marginally better sometimes it does marginally worse
claims.claim: Machine-learning models often do only marginally better or worse than simple existing trend models; simple benchmarks are hard to beat.
claims.testable: yes - ML vs simple trend benchmark out of sample

claims.speaker: Cem Karsan (captioned 'Jim')
claims.quote: the way we tend to use it is not for intelligence as the name implies but really as uh as workers
claims.claim: AI is useful as a worker for aggregating data and drafting basic code, lowering costs, not for solving core quantitative problems.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the AI models were exactly as bad as the doctors um in terms of interpreting the data
claims.claim: In a hospital study on proprietary data AI was no better than doctors at reading radiology, suggesting AI may not improve on human judgement with noisy data.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: really is just going to be picking up and amplifying on the biases that we know exist
claims.claim: Given poor financial data and gaming, AI in investing will likely amplify known biases, while systematic trend models keep an edge because humans are poor market timers.
claims.testable: partly - check AI fund performance in 3-5 years

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: Divergence between fed uh fed behavior in September and then the bond market
claims.claim: In 2024 the Fed cut from September yet long yields rose, so assuming policy cuts shift the whole curve down conflated macro trends with market trends.
claims.indicator: Fed funds vs long Treasury yields
claims.testable: yes - curve moves after first cuts

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the biggest mistakes is people trying to anticipate uh fed policy and sort of having sort of swinging back and forth between expectations
claims.claim: Trying to anticipate Fed policy as expectations swung was the main source of losses in 2024 for trend and other investors.

claims.speaker: unclear (unattributed in captions)
claims.quote: the beauty about Trend following is that it never makes any mistakes it's never wrong because we're not trying to predict anything
claims.claim: Trend following makes no forecasts, only follows prices, so it cannot make prediction mistakes ('prices are primal').

claims.speaker: unclear (unattributed in captions)
claims.quote: I increased my location to Trend following it what turned out to be pretty close to a local maximum
claims.claim: Discretionary increases in trend-following allocation tend to be timed near local performance peaks, even when the system itself behaves correctly.
claims.testable: partly - investor flow timing vs CTA returns

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: it's ranged basically year to date uh between you know maybe 70% for the year down to you know minus 5% for the year
claims.claim: Trend-follower returns in 2024 ranged from about +70% to about -5%, and benchmarks like the SG Trend index mostly reflect the largest managers, questioning a single trend beta.
claims.indicator: IASG trend manager returns; SG Trend index

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: return dispersion is sort of always underestimated by clients in our space because we all have very high correlation but the range of outcomes are very large
claims.claim: Trend managers are highly correlated yet their return outcomes vary widely because parameter choices make time-series patterns diverge.

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: we were in a period where the long-term trends seemed to be more clear but shorter term undulations
claims.claim: 2024 dispersion was mostly by time horizon: long-term trends were clear while short-term swings around rate and political regime changes punished faster models.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: number one is speed Katie mentioned it I mentioned it earlier number two is Universe
claims.claim: Trend manager returns differ for three reasons, speed, universe and purity (trend vs reversion/carry add-ons), plus discretionary de-risking.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I cannot give zero probability on a systematic manager basically calling the shorts over the weekend
claims.claim: Some nominally systematic managers likely de-risked discretionarily around the August 2024 payrolls/BoJ weekend, adding to dispersion.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the dispersion this year I think it primarily comes from the speed
claims.claim: 2024 trend dispersion came mainly from speed, then universe and purity, since cross-sectional reversion did well in both 2023 and 2024.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: small changes in in in parameters would not only result in big near-term dispersion depending on which markets we're over waiting under waiting how we're sizing positions
claims.claim: Small parameter changes in simple bank trend models produced large and persistent return dispersion, which led to using simpler top-down replication for stability.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I don't see it meaningfully larger than other years
claims.claim: He does not see 2024 trend dispersion as meaningfully larger than usual; wide dispersion is the normal state.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: I've always used the sort of what I call the uh you know a three Factor model I call it uh STM style timing in markets
claims.claim: Classifying trend followers by style, timing (speed) and markets removes much of the apparent dispersion; much dispersion is a classification problem.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you have some kind of limitation on uh the total number of uh contracts you hold uh then [L600] for a a you know multi-billion dollar uh fund
claims.claim: Large trend funds could not get meaningful exposure to small markets like coffee and cocoa because of contract/position limits, so size contributed to 2024 dispersion.
